page.layout: One printed page, a single column of italic verse in seven stanzas of four lines, indented in turn. Running head at top right, page number at top left, catchword at lower right. Faint show-through from the other side on the right.

p.i: Quæ grata sedes, quæ tua ciuitas Dilecta quondam, nunc lapidum iacet Turpes acerui, nunc sepulta est Ipsa suis Solymæ ruinis.
Passim piorum strata cadauera Sunt esca cælifassa[?] volucribus, Carnesque sanctorum tuorum Præda feris, canibusque terræ,
Fluxere rivi sanguinis undique, Ut vilis undæ flumina per vias Proiecta, nec vili repertus Corpora qui tegeret sepulcro.
Turpis propinquis fabula gentibus, Turpis per vrbes finitimas locus Facti fumus, quis finis irae? Quo tuus usque vorax ut ignis
Ardebit, ô Rex, horribilis furor? Exerce in illum sœuitiam tui Cœtum flagelli, rite qui te Nosse negat, negat invocare.
Nam deuorarunt fauctibus impijs Carnes Iacobi. Cinibus oppida Agri colonis, templa vasis Quæque suis spoliata lugent.
Ne pristinarum, ne memor amplius Sis noxiarum, quas tibi fecimus, Extrema sed passis malorum Ferre pius propera lenamen[?].

page.notes: Stanza breaks follow the four-line pattern of the printed verse. Line 6, "cælifassa[?]", is doubtful: the word is set in a long-s ligature and I could not read it with certainty. Line 28, "lenamen[?]", appears to read so in print; it may be a printing error for "levamen", left as printed. Line 3 "acerui" and line 23 "vasis" are read from the long-s forms and are otherwise clear. The faint text on the right is show-through from the reverse and is omitted.
